title: What Qualcomm Has Stopped Leading With
detail:
What Qualcomm Has Stopped Leading With
Trefis Team
Wed, September 9, 2026 at 12:50 PM CDT 3 min read
QCOM
MSFT
AVGO
AMD
INTC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Qualcomm (QCOM) has spent years telling shareholders it is becoming more than a smartphone chip company. What changed is where the new growth is expected to come from. Two years ago the big non-handset targets were automotive and IoT. Today, the newest leg of the story runs through the data center, and management has already put a number on it.

Qualcomm Once Told You The Laptop Chip Had Redefined Computing

The Snapdragon X Series was the flagship of that older story. Two years ago management said those platforms had redefined personal computing.

Management no longer leads with that story. In the fiscal Q3 2026 call, delivered on July 29, 2026, the PC gets two passing lines: a growing share of design wins in AI-first laptops and Project Solara, a chip-to-cloud platform being built with Microsoft for agent-first enterprise devices. Both are real. Neither carries a revenue figure.

Qualcomm Nearly Doubled Its Non-Handset Target Without Naming The Laptop

Management raised its fiscal 2029 non-handset revenue outlook to $40 billion, up from a previous $22 billion target that covered combined automotive and IoT. The new figure rests on two named legs: more than $24 billion across automotive and IoT, and more than $15 billion in data center. Company revenue over the past twelve months was about $44 billion, so the fiscal 2029 non-handset target alone is close to the whole business today.

Qualcomm calls itself a new entrant in the data center. Two custom silicon wins turn revenue-generating in the December quarter, the opening quarter of a fiscal 2027 in which management forecasts $5 billion of data center revenue. That early revenue, mostly custom chip engagements, comes in significantly below the base business on margin, a drag management sizes at 1.5% to 2% on the weighted average gross margin of QCT, Qualcomm's chip segment.

That reweighting lands while overall growth is soft. Revenue grew 1.9% over the past twelve months against a three-year average pace of 4.8%. QCT gross margins are guided slightly below their historical range on higher input costs, with price increases expected to pull them back up.

You Have Seen Qualcomm Win A New Market Before, In The Car

The counterweight is automotive, and it is already revenue. Fiscal Q3 2026 automotive sales were a record $1.6 billion, up 61% year over year, and management raised the annualized run rate it expects as fiscal 2026 ends to about $7 billion from $6 billion. An expanded BMW agreement made Qualcomm the lead compute silicon provider for that carmaker's next-generation ADAS and digital cockpit.

title: Palantir Changed The Number It Wants You To Judge It By
detail:
Palantir Changed The Number It Wants You To Judge It By

Image from Pixabay

Palantir Technologies (PLTR) used to report its total customer count on the quarterly earnings call. The latest call did not include it. In the count's place sits a bookings figure large enough to change what kind of business you are looking at, and the swap says more about what a holder owns than the headline growth rates do.

Palantir Used To Give A Company-Wide Customer Count On Its Earnings Calls

As recently as the first quarter of 2026 that count stood at 1,007. Counts were the pitch well before that: in the third quarter of 2024 management put U.S. commercial customers at 321, and a rising base was the proof that AIP, the company's AI platform, had found buyers outside the government work Palantir grew up on.

The second quarter of 2026 earnings call carries no company-wide count at all. The only one management still gives is the U.S. commercial figure, which counts a narrower population, at 653. There was no announcement that the company-wide count was being retired. The count simply stopped being a metric Palantir used to lead with.

Now Palantir Leads With The Value Of Contracts It Has Signed

What took its place is total contract value. In the second quarter of 2026, Palantir signed $2.132 billion of U.S. commercial bookings, up 153% year over year, and $5.964 billion over the past twelve months, against the company's $6.16 billion of revenue over the past twelve months. That value spreads across multi-year contracts, so it measures commitment ahead of revenue.

Set the count and the revenue beside each other, and the shape is plain. Over the past year the U.S. commercial customer count grew 35%. U.S. commercial revenue grew 149%. Revenue per customer is climbing far faster than the customer list, and net dollar retention across the company of 157% shows existing accounts expanding at the same time.

Management explains the expansion as customers climbing its own stack. Accounts that were only using Foundry now want Ontology and the whole sovereign AI stack, and that expansion lands in bookings long before it lands in revenue. Since the quarter closed, in early September 2026, Palantir widened its PwC alliance to push enterprise AI deeper inside big organizations.

What You Own Now Rides On How Big Each Account Gets

None of this reads as trouble. Revenue grew 93% year over year in the second quarter of 2026, the fastest Palantir has ever reported, and management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a midpoint of $8.154 billion, its largest full-year raise ever. If a rising outlook is what you are buying, our guidance-driven momentum screen tracks who is actually lifting one.

title: Defiance Politely Asks the SEC to Let It Sell An ETF 8-Ball
detail:
Defiance Politely Asks the SEC to Let It Sell An ETF 8-Ball
Thornton McEnery

NVDA

PLTR
GOOG

Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Defiance Politely Asks the SEC to Let It Sell An ETF 8-Ball - Moby
THE GIST

Our analysts just identified a stock with the potential to be the next Nvidia. Tell us how you invest and we'll show you why it's our #1 pick. Tap here.

There is a moment in every wild party where somebody suggests a new thing that will make the night 10 times more fun for 45 minutes and excruciatingly worse for the days that will follow. Defiance ETFs has decided that we've reached that point in the ETF party and just filed its suggestion with the Securities and Exchange Commission… Sixteen times over.

WHAT HAPPENED

Defiance wants to launch 16 new ETFs, all built on the same idea and all named for it: the Defiance 2X Hourly Reset ETF, one each for NVDA, TSLA, PLTR, GOOG, META, MSFT, AMD, MU, TSM, MRVL and six more. Paperwork went in through Tidal Trust V with the clock set to run 75 days, so they go live around November 4 unless somebody stops them.

Each fund promises double whatever the stock does, and then delivers on that promise six separate times a day. Every roughly hour-long window starts fresh, with the leverage reset to 2x from wherever the stock happens to be sitting. The filing says outright that the promise applies to nothing else. Not to a day, not to a month, not to a year. Six windows, and after each one closes, whatever happened in it is permanent.

Your losses don't get a fresh start when the leverage does. A stock that whipsaws its way to nowhere by 4 p.m. can leave the fund substantially poorer, and every additional reset is another chance for that to happen.

Defiance gets its exposure mostly through swaps, then short-dated options, and will hold the stock outright on margin when the derivatives dry up. Between 40% and 60% of the fund sits parked as collateral rather than doing anything. Each reset skims a basis point on whatever gets traded. Six times a day, 252 days a year, that adds up to a toll nobody notices individually.

WHY IT MATTERS

Getting back to the party analogy, Defiance has clearly recognized this is the inflection point in the ETF frenzy where the drugs are starting to wear off and the anhedonia is creeping in, leaving the more devoted party animals to chase a new high. So Defiance just asked the SEC if it would be cool to drop an 8-ball on the table and see who's down.

Unlike an 8-ball though, this comes with a warning label. Buried in the filing is a table showing what a holder loses when the stock finishes the year exactly where it started. At 25% annualized volatility, down 6.1%. At 75%, down 43%. At 100% volatility on a stock that went nowhere, down 63.2%.

title: Alphabet's ROIC Is Strong, but Is GOOGL Stock a Buy Now?
detail:
Alphabet's ROIC Is Strong, but Is GOOGL Stock a Buy Now?
Rimmi Singhi
Wed, September 9, 2026 at 10:57 AM CDT 4 min read
GOOG
AMZN
MSFT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Alphabet GOOGL is one of the most influential players in the technology sector. Google Search and YouTube provide a durable advertising engine, while Google Cloud is becoming an increasingly important growth and profit driver. Now, the company is pouring massive amounts of capital into artificial intelligence to strengthen its position in the AI race. That might lead investors to wonder if Alphabet's strong returns on capital are enough to justify its rising investment needs.

Strong ROIC Reflects a High-Quality Business

Return on invested capital (ROIC) measures how effectively a company generates operating profit from the capital invested in its business. A higher ROIC indicates that a company can create more value from each dollar committed to operations.

Alphabet's numbers stand out. Its trailing-12-month (TTM) ROIC is 40.36%, more than double its 10-year median of 20.3% and above the 20% industry median.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Its one-year, three-year and five-year medians of 29.8%, 27.4% and 26%, respectively, also demonstrate a sustained improvement in capital efficiency.

The underlying business underscores Alphabet's strong ROIC. Google Search & other revenues rose 17% year over year to $63.27 billion in the second quarter of 2026, while YouTube advertising revenues increased 13% to $11.06 billion. At the same time, Google Cloud revenues surged 82% to $24.77 billion, with operating margin expanding to 35.6% from 20.7%.

Cloud also has a substantial runway, with backlog reaching $514 billion. Meanwhile, Gemini adoption and Alphabet's broader AI stack are creating additional opportunities across Search, enterprise software, infrastructure and security.

Earnings Quality Remains a Major Strength

In the trailing four quarters, Alphabet surpassed earnings estimates on all occasions.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Alphabet also scores well on earnings consistency. Per our proprietary model, Alphabet has a 93.9% 10-year earnings linearity, which is close to the 100% ideal and far above the 46.9% industry median. This consistency reflects the strength of Search, expanding YouTube monetization and the growing contribution from Cloud. On a TTM basis, our model calculates a 10-year EPS CAGR of 26.5%.

But strong earnings and returns tell only part of the story— how that profit converts to cash is where the picture changes.

The Cash Conversion Problem

Our proprietary calculation shows that Alphabet's TTM cash-flow conversion— operating cash flow relative to net income— is 76.1%, below its 105.8% median, while FCF conversion (which measures free cash flow against net income) is only 21.8% versus a 43% median. The deterioration largely reflects the enormous resources being committed to AI infrastructure and related working-capital requirements.
